description.narrative: The Project will develop value chains to deliver unique premium value products to niche markets. The Project will deliver these outputs through three components: (i) value-chain development under which it will establish a deposit account to guarantee 50% of the total amount of loans made by private commercial banks to agribusiness enterprises for value-chain development investment plans (selected by the bank from among a group of prequalified plans with high public goods elements), (ii) a local grant and infrastructure development facility to develop rural infrastructure and services, and (iii) project management. In a break with traditional approaches, the Project will provide private enterprises with resources to undertake value-chain investments that have typically been undertaken by public agencies.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Production capacity of herders and farmers improved Indicator: 120 herder and farmer cooperatives supported by the project increase their outputs by at least 20% by Q4 2020 (added; 2015 baseline: 104) Progress/Status: During the original (Grant 0115-MON) project PMU disbursed USD1,457,523.45 in 176 grants to 104 cooperatives and veterinary and breeding centers represented by 2,286 member households. RID team completion report states that vet services centers that received grants increased their revenue in 2012 on average by 28% compared to FY 2010, Marketing Coops by 27% and Fodder Production coops by 21% respectively.As of 31 March 2019, beekeeping (13) and fiber (5) cooperatives supported by the TA were increased their honey production output by 42.5% and 66% respectively compared to 2017. However TA is currently supporting 28 cooperatives which exceed the planned target number of cooperatives by 57.1% under the current project. Data Source: Cooperative survey Actual value:

Output: VCIs financed Indicator: About 80 VCIs are financed by Q4 2020 (changed; 2015 baseline: 12) Progress/Status: As of 30 June 2019, 30 VCI subloans have been approved by ADB. Data Source: Signed subloan agreements from PMU Actual value:

Output: VCIs financed Indicator: Due diligence of about 80 VCI subprojects is completed by Q3 2020 (added; 2015 baseline: 16) Progress/Status: As of 30 June 2019, due diligence for 30 VCI subprojects have been approved by ADB. Data Source: Due diligence documents of the VCI subprojects from PMU Actual value:

Output: VCIs financed Indicator: 800 person-times of PPE staff and 120 person-times of PPB staff are trained on finance, safeguards, gender, and monitoring by Q2 2020, of which at least 40% are women (added; 2015 baseline: 300 and 32) Progress/Status: 1,415 person-times of PPE staff and 714 person-times of PPB staff (including Credit Guarantee Fund staff) were trained on finance, safeguards, gender, and monitoring of which 1,051 or 49.4% are women. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports from PMU Actual value:

Output: Enterprises' marketing and technical capacity improved Indicator: 800 person-times of PPE staff, of which at least 40% are female, are trained on marketing and technical skills by Q4 2020 (added; 2015 baseline: 350) Progress/Status: (i) During the Original project 350 people attended training activities under Output 3, of 160 or 45.7% are female. (ii) During the ARDP AF 1,064 person-times of PPE staff were trained, of which 72.9% are women. Due to the additional subsectors (apparel, bee-farm, meat and sea-buckthorn) are covered by the current TA project, the number of participants will be increased.
As of end of the reporting period all together 1,414 people were trained, of which 936 or 66.2% are female.
Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Production capacity of herders and farmers improved Indicator: 5,500 person-times of herders, farmers, primary processors, and relevant technical staff of local governments, of which 40% are women, trained by Q4 2019 (added; 2015 baseline: 4,320) Progress/Status: Training ongoing Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports from PMU Actual value:

Output: Enterprises' marketing and technical capacity improved Indicator: Target market analysis for leather subsector is completed by Q4 2019 (added) Progress/Status: Ongoing Data Source: Target market analysis report for leather subsector Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: Enterprises' marketing and technical capacity improved Indicator: Technical guidelines for enterprises of animal fiber and leather subsectors are developed by Q4 2019 (added) Progress/Status: In 2018, target PPEs were trained on developing required technical guidelines and topics for technical guidelines were identified. Actual development of guidelines will take place in 2019 and required budget is included in the annual workplan accordingly. Preparation activities are ongoing. Currently training on codes of practice in fiber harvesting for herders and knitwear trials for PPEs at production level were conducted. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Export-oriented PPEs increase their export share in total sales by 20% on average (added) c. PPEs generate 1,800 new jobs, of which at least 40% are to be filled by women (added; 2015 baseline: 1,150) Progress/Status: To be measured at project completion.
